$comment: Every \source{key} in the book resolves here, and tools/check_sources.py
fails the build when one does not.
The `quality` field is the load-bearing part, not the URL. A claim about
what the market does is only as good as the thing it rests on, and this
field is what lets check_sources.py refuse a confident sentence built on
one person's blog post.
strong         several independent sources, or a dataset with a stated method
moderate       one good source, corroborated in outline elsewhere
single-source  one source only; a \reported{} citing this must say so
unverified     traced only to content-marketing; may be used ONLY in
Appendix C, as an example of a claim this kit refuses
`read` records whether the claim was checked against the source itself or
through a second hand. That distinction is not decoration: several primary
sources below were unreachable from the machine this kit was written on,
and a summary of a source is not the source.
primary        the source itself was read
secondary      read through coverage or search summaries only
`accessed` is the date the entry was last checked. An entry with no date
is a claim nobody has dated, which is the shape of every stale fact.
--- Entries below exist ONLY so Appendix C can name what it refuses. ---
A \reported{} may not cite these. check_sources.py enforces it.

field-guide.title: AI Engineering Field Guide
field-guide.author: Alexey Grigorev
field-guide.method: Aggregated from roughly 6,964 scraped job descriptions across six regions, 51 companies with a disclosed interview process, and more than 100 take-home repositories. One author's methodology, so a figure appearing only here is one measurement rather than a consensus - but it is a stated method over a named corpus, which is more than anything else in this space offers.

field-guide-system-design.title: AI system design questions
field-guide-system-design.note: This file and the get-hired file disagree about whether observability is a featured interview topic. The disagreement is inside one corpus and is reported in chapter 36 rather than resolved.

aie-book.title: AI Engineering
aie-book.author: Chip Huyen
aie-book.note: Used for the boundary between AI engineering and classical machine learning: AI engineering starts from available models and prototypes early; classical ML starts from data, features and training.

coderpad-hiring-2026.title: State of Tech Hiring 2026
coderpad-hiring-2026.note: A vendor's own survey of hiring leaders, and the sample size was not retrieved. Used only for the coarse split - roughly half permit AI in technical rounds, a fifth decide case by case, and the rest do not - and the sentence that cites it says it is one survey.

canva-ai-interviews.title: Yes, You Can Use AI in Our Interviews. In fact, we insist
canva-ai-interviews.note: The company's own post, so the claim about its own practice is primary in principle - but it was unreachable from this machine and is corroborated only through trade coverage.

sierra-ai-native-interview.title: The AI-native interview
sierra-ai-native-interview.note: The clearest published description of a two-hour AI-assisted build round with a plan phase before it and a review phase after. Unreachable from this machine; reconstructed from search summaries and the author's own social post.

etsy-ladder.title: Engineering Career Ladder
etsy-ladder.note: A published ladder, which is what makes it usable: the wording can be quoted rather than paraphrased. The load-bearing word for Staff is "unscoped".

progression-fyi.title: progression.fyi
progression-fyi.note: An aggregator of open engineering ladders. Use it to read several rather than trusting one.

archetypes-rebuttal-goedecke.title: Why I don't like the staff engineer archetypes
archetypes-rebuttal-goedecke.author: Sean Goedecke
archetypes-rebuttal-goedecke.note: The published disagreement matters more than either position. Chapter 03 carries both.

being-glue.title: Being Glue
being-glue.author: Tanya Reilly
being-glue.note: The canonical treatment of work that is necessary, invisible to the ladder, and not promotable.

meta-ai-enabled-coding.title: Meta's AI-enabled coding interview
meta-ai-enabled-coding.note: Two prep sites describe this round and both trace to the same leaked internal note, so it is one source wearing two hats. It is also the most decision-relevant claim in the research - that at the more senior levels the AI-assisted round replaces the AI-free one rather than joining it. Any sentence citing this must say it is one source.

google-code-comprehension.title: Google's AI-assisted coding interview
google-code-comprehension.note: A prep vendor, but it quotes a named executive on the record, which is more than the rest of that genre offers.

hamel-llm-judge.title: Creating a LLM-as-a-Judge that drives business results
hamel-llm-judge.author: Hamel Husain

kalra-transition.title: From software engineer to AI engineer
kalra-transition.author: Janvi Kalra
kalra-transition.note: One engineer's account of roughly 46 interviews over six months. The segmentation into product, infrastructure and model companies is the most actionable idea in it; the frequently-quoted figure about how many senior loops contain no algorithmic coding is one observer's sample and is refused in Appendix C.

mcp-prompt-injection.title: Prompt injection in MCP: tool poisoning and blast radius

agentic-injection.title: From LLM to agentic AI: prompt injection got worse
agentic-injection.author: Christian Schneider

refused-comp-premium.title: AI engineering roles command a 25-40 per cent premium
refused-comp-premium.url: (a single blog post, no method stated)
refused-comp-premium.refused_because: One post, no methodology, no corpus, no date range. Widely repeated, never sourced.

refused-no-algorithms.title: Around seventy per cent of senior loops contain no algorithmic coding
refused-no-algorithms.url: (traced to one engineer's account of her own interviews)
refused-no-algorithms.refused_because: One observer, a self-selected set of companies, one point in time. It is quoted as a base rate and is not one.

refused-staff-proportion.title: Fewer than ten per cent of engineers reach Staff
refused-staff-proportion.refused_because: No population, no ladder, no counting method.

refused-named-loops.title: Named frontier labs' interview loops, stage by stage
refused-named-loops.refused_because: Every version found was a vendor page citing anonymous reports. Some of it is plausibly fabricated, and a candidate who prepares against a fabricated loop prepares for nothing.
